steps.description: We will read `Transmuter.sol` top-to-bottom, stopping at every major concept: dependencies, constants, storage layout, constructor configuration, access control, administrative setters, metadata helpers, the redemption lifecycle, graph queries, and the private helpers that bind everything together.

Dependencies. ❶ IAlchemistV3 – external engine used to convert synthetic debt ↔️ yield tokens. ❷ StakingGraph – Fenwick tree library that tracks aggregate stake weight per block. ❸ TokenUtils – safe token helpers, and ❹ NFTMetadataGenerator – ERC-721 metadata.  OpenZeppelin’s ERC721 and utils are inherited for the NFT wrapper.

Three numerical constants govern fee maths and graph scaling. 26: BPS – basis-points denominator (=10 000). 27: FIXED_POINT_SCALAR – 1e18 fixed-point helper when comparing debt and collateral units. 28: BLOCK_SCALING_FACTOR – 1e8 magnifier that turns fractional stake-per-block into signed ints with enough precision for the Fenwick tree.

Public state layout. 34-49 configurable economics (depositCap, fees, graphSize, timeToTransmute). 52-58 admin & fee receiver. 61 syntheticToken holds the alAsset ERC-20. 64 live alchemist instance and 67 a list of earlier ones. 70-76 private bookkeeping – individual StakingPositions, the Fenwick graph, and the NFT nonce.
Constructor wires the parameters struct into storage. All knobs (fees, cap, graphSize, timing) are fixed at deployment; admin starts as the deployer.
onlyAdmin modifier – every administrative call funnels through _checkArgument to guarantee msg.sender == admin.
Guard helpers: _checkArgument (lines 275-279) & _checkState (283-288) revert with custom IllegalArgument / IllegalState when a pre-condition fails.
Admin hand-over. setPendingAdmin stores a new candidate; acceptAdmin validates sender == pendingAdmin then flips admin and clears the slot, emitting events.

Economic knobs. Each setter checks bounds then updates storage and emits an event: setAlchemist, setDepositCap (requires cap fits into int256 for graph maths), setTransmutationFee & setExitFee (≤BPS), setTransmutationTime, setProtocolFeeReceiver (non-zero).
Read-only helpers. tokenURI composes on-chain metadata through NFTMetadataGenerator; getPosition exposes the raw StakingPosition struct.

createRedemption lifecycle. 173-179 guards: non-zero deposit & within depositCap and outstanding synthetic supply. 185 transfers the alAsset from user. 187 stores a new StakingPosition keyed by ++_nonce. 190 updates the Fenwick graph with per-block weight = amount × SCALE ÷ duration. 192-195 totals locked and mints the ERC-721 to caller. 196 emits PositionCreated.

claimRedemption unwinds a position. Steps: 202 existence check. 208-211 calculate matured vs. remaining amount. 212 owner check then burn NFT. 219-224 redeem yield from Alchemist only if local balance is insufficient. 225-230 compute transmutation & exit fees. 233 removes residual stake from graph. 235-242 bad-debt ratio scales down claim if system is underwater. 243-248 transfers yield tokens & synthetic tokens, splitting fees. 250 burns the fully transmuted synths. 252-256 update totals, emit event, delete storage.
queryGraph uses StakingGraph.queryStake to pull the aggregate stake weight over a block window, then converts back from scaled int to debt token units (+1 for rounding).

`StakingGraph.addStake` packs two delta updates (`amount` and `amount×block`) into a **Fenwick tree**, expanding the tree size when necessary. `Transmuter` passes `amount × SCALE ÷ duration` so every stake contributes a constant weight per block.
`StakingGraph.queryStake` subtracts prefix sums of (`Δ`, `Δ×block`) to retrieve the exact weight between start & end. This is the primitive used by `Transmuter.queryGraph`.
`_updateStakingGraph` is merely a thin wrapper calling `addStake` with current block and the chosen duration, keeping library code encapsulated.

You can now follow every storage write and library call from `deposit`, through `maturation`, to `claim`, and understand how the **Fenwick graph** lets anyone preview upcoming liquidity needs with `queryGraph`.
